Subject: Consent to Service, Emergency Relief Carveout & Governing Law Proposal

Elena —

Thanks for sending the draft Order Form. We reviewed the MSA redlines (attached) and wanted to surface three items that will determine execution timing. Keeping this tight so we can lock the order form and kick off onboarding next week: 

1) Governing law / jurisdiction: our standard is Delaware law for the MSA, with an arbitration-first dispute resolution clause for covered disputes.

2) Emergency injunctive relief carveout: we are open to a carveout that allows NorthBridge to obtain temporary injunctive relief in local courts to preserve urgent customer data or prevent exfiltration, but we need clear consent-to-service and a narrow definition to avoid defeat of the arbitration process.

3) Consent to service / service agents: for companies outside the U.S. we sometimes accept a consent-to-service clause or an agreed agent for service. For U.S.-based buyers we typically ask for either consent to service in Delaware or acceptance of notice by registered agent.

Proposed package (short):
- Governing law: Delaware law.
- Dispute resolution: binding arbitration (JAMS or AAA) for covered disputes; exceptions: either party may seek emergency injunctive relief in state or federal court as necessary to preserve rights (IP or data security).
- Consent to service: buyer consents to service of process in Delaware (or appoints Delaware agent).

If NorthBridge needs a different seat for arbitration we can consider a neutral forum but would like Delaware law to apply. Can you confirm whether NorthBridge will accept: (a) Delaware law, (b) arbitration with injunctive relief carveout, and (c) consent to service or registered agent?

I've attached a redline of the MSA showing the exact language we propose: Redwood_MSA_redline_20280822.pdf (redline key on page 2).

Thanks —
Naomi

Naomi —

Appreciate the clarity and the redline. A few quick points from our side after a rapid check with counsel: 

- Governing law: we prefer New York law for commercial predictability; Delaware would be acceptable only if the seat of arbitration is also in the U.S. and certain consumer-facing carveouts are narrowed.
- Arbitration seat: we would like arbitration to be seated in New York (if arbitration is insisted on).
- Injunctive relief carveout: we need an explicit statement that injunctive relief may be sought in any court of competent jurisdiction (not limited to Delaware) when immediate action is needed to stop data exfiltration. Our security team requires this for SOC2 gating.
- Consent to service: NorthBridge cannot accept broad automatic consent to service in Delaware. We can accept a U.S. agent for service or explicit service-by-email plus a commercial agent in New York.

Would Redwood accept the following compromise?
- Governing law: New York (commercial contract law).
- Disputes: binding arbitration (AAA) seated in New York; emergency injunctive relief allowed in any court where NorthBridge has a real and substantial connection (including local courts) — Redwood retains right to seek temporary relief in Delaware courts if we notify and provide jurisdictional consent.
- Service: accept service by designated registered agent in New York or service via counsel plus certified email to contracts@redwood.com.

If those terms are a hard no from your side, we can loop in procurement legal to escalate. We are motivated to move quickly; onboarding target is 9/5.

Best,
Elena Morales
Head of Procurement
NorthBridge AI
elena@northbridge.ai

Elena / Naomi —

Thanks for the notes. Quick legal perspective and a proposed compromise we think is practical and preserves the benefits of arbitration while satisfying NorthBridge's SOC2/security gating concerns: 

1) Governing law: Redwood prefers Delaware for corporate predictability and our precedent; New York is acceptable if NorthBridge insists, but we would ask for express carveouts to preserve our enforcement rights. 

2) Injunctive relief carveout (compromise language): 
- Covered disputes remain in arbitration.
- Notwithstanding arbitration, either party may seek emergency injunctive relief in any court of competent jurisdiction to prevent immediate and irreparable harm (including data exfiltration).
- If relief is sought outside Delaware (or outside seat), the party seeking relief must: (i) provide notice to the other party and (ii) agree that any subsequent relief on the merits will remain subject to the arbitration agreement. This avoids forum-shopping for final relief while permitting urgent local temporary remedies.

3) Consent to service / service agent: 
- If NorthBridge will not accept Delaware consent-to-service, we will accept registration of a U.S. registered agent in New York for service (reasonable) OR an agreed process where service to counsel plus contracts@redwood.com with 5 business days cure constitutes effective service.

4) Practical tweaks: specify AAA (or JAMS) and allow either party to apply to a local court for interim measures. Add a short clause that any interim court measures do not waive arbitration for the merits.

If that looks workable for you, Naomi — please propose a single redline we can send back. Elena — if you want, we can mark the exact paragraph language for the injunctive carveout and service clause and share a clean vs redline.

Rishi
Senior Counsel, Contracts

Rishi / Naomi —

Thanks — that compromise gets us close. Two final asks from NorthBridge counsel before we can sign: 

1) Add a 14-day notice-and-cure window for any temporary injunctive filing except in cases where the notice would materially frustrate preservation of evidence (i.e., active exfiltration). That helps our GC run a rapid internal check before external filings.

2) For service: we will register a New York agent for process AND agree to service-by-email to contracts@redwood.com provided Redwood acknowledges receipt within 3 business days (we need that confirmation to unblock procurement).

If you can accept those two items, I’ll get an updated signature block and the Order Form executed by EOD Friday. We’re aligned on seat and law (New York) if you prefer to move the choice of law to New York — otherwise we can keep Delaware if Redwood sends final redline.

Elena
